items.title: ABHI UK HealthTech Conference 2026, London, 9 to 10 November
items.summary: ABHI's flagship two-day conference runs 9 to 10 November 2026 at the Cavendish Conference Centre, London. Day one covers regulation, MHRA early engagement, AI oversight and post-market surveillance.

items.title: GPs report disruption to IT systems and referrals amid Microsoft outage
items.summary: GP practices across the UK are reporting disruption to IT systems and referrals amid an ongoing global Microsoft outage. Practices have been notifying patients that the outage is causing issues in receiving and replying to emails, as well as delays in receiving and processing hospital correspondence and referrals.

items.title: Leeds Community calls for views of local service users on use of AI in community services
items.summary: Leeds Community Healthcare NHS Trust is inviting local service users to have their say on the use of AI in community services. Anyone who uses LCH community NHS services in Leeds is welcome to take part, the trust says, with recruitment open until January 2027.

items.title: Great Western pilots mobile diagnostic service in the community
items.summary: Great Western Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust has shared details of a new mobile diagnostic service bringing X-rays, ultrasound, invitro diagnostics and urinary tract infection testing directly to patients in the community, with aims to avoid unnecessary journeys and admissions to hospital.

items.title: General practice staff in Wales trained to use AI tool
items.summary: General practice staff in Wales were among more than 6,000 NHS Wales employees to receive training on using the artificial intelligence (AI) tool Microsoft Copilot in their everyday work.

items.title: GPs keen to add data to Palantir platform, company suggested to health minister
items.summary: US tech company Palantir contacted a health minister about the benefits of adding GP patient data to its national health data tool, documents have revealed.

items.title: Croydon Health Services sets out AI use cases across discharge planning, virtual wards, documentation, referral triage, imaging
items.summary: Croydon Health Services NHS Trust inaugural AI strategy has set out a range of use cases from HR processes to clinical coding, and from contract management to diagnostics and clinical decision support.

items.title: Barts Health project sees AI eye-tracking tech to help patients with speech difficulties communicate
items.summary: A project developed at Barts Health NHS Trust is using AI eye-tracking technology to help patients with speech difficulties to communicate.

items.title: Innovation brief: women’s health, paediatric insomnia, AI funding
items.summary: In this news in brief article, we take a look at some of the latest around international innovations, covering women’s health, paediatric insomnia, AI, and wearables.

items.title: Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS on cloud, AI, EPRs, Copilot, cyber security
items.summary: In its latest annual report on digital, Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust has highlighted benefits and outcomes from digital initiatives such as the migration of over 300 servers and systems to new data centres, the implementation of new software for mental health documentation, and a pilot of…

items.title: Lincolnshire Partnership seeks input from service users on functionality for new patient app
items.summary: Lincolnshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust has launched a survey seeking views on its upcoming patient engagement portal, with questions around desired functionality across electronic appointment management, accessing information about care and treatment, and sending and receiving secure messages.

items.title: Award: Post-Deployment Monitoring of Diagnostic Imaging Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the NHS
items.summary: NHS England. Contract awarded to the Royal College of Radiologists (RCR) to undertake a discovery project to determine national post-deployment monitoring (PDM) of AI diagnostic tools in the NHS.

items.title: Automating medicine management at University Hospitals of Liverpool Group
items.summary: University Hospitals of Liverpool Group has introduced automated medicine management, supporting an aim for safer and efficient medicines processes. In a partnership with BD, automated dispensing cabinets will be installed in 48 clinical areas over the next two years at Aintree University Hospital.

items.title: DHCW shares new dataset and automation to improve use of urgent and emergency care data
items.summary: Digital Health and Care Wales is taking steps to improve the recording and use of urgent and emergency care data, with a timeline put forward for the implementation of the Welsh Emergency Care Data Set (WECDS), and the automation of reporting through the National Data Resource.

items.title: £40 million programme for proactive care and admission prevention ahead of winter 2026/27
items.summary: The UK government has announced a £40 million programme designed to support up to 300,000 patients identified as being vulnerable this winter with additional GP support, in an attempt to reduce avoidable hospital admissions and provide proactive care to those with conditions such as heart disease or frailty.

items.title: Times of change in NHS patient safety: the march of AI
items.summary: John Tingle, Associate Professor, Birmingham Law School, University of Birmingham, discusses some recent NHS patient safety publications considering the role of AI in the NHS and the implications of its…

items.title: Developing a digital knowledge-to-practice framework for urinary device management and CAUTI surveillance
items.summary: Background: Inappropriate urinary device use and catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) contribute to preventable patient harm, antimicrobial resistance, incontinence-associated dermatitis (IAD) and prolonged hospitalisation.

items.title: South East Coast Ambulance Service presents findings from “PARA-AI” project exploring attitudes toward AI in pre-hospital care
items.summary: South East Coast Ambulance (SECAmb) Service NHS Foundation Trust has presented findings from its “PARA-AI” project exploring attitudes toward AI in pre-hospital care, finding strong support for AI use in clinical care with the appropriate safeguards.

items.title: People strategy from Royal Free London sets future workforce and digital readiness
items.summary: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust has launched its people strategy to 2031 noting digital, data, and automation as a key enabler in reshaping how care and work are delivered, committing to keeping people “at the heart” of rapid change.

items.title: 10-year £12m EPR contract awarded by South London and Maudsley
items.summary: A ten-year EPR contract has been awarded to The Access Group by South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust. The contract, worth an estimated £11.9 million, will run from November 2026 to November 2036. It was reportedly awarded via the NHS LPP clinical digital health solutions framework agreement.

items.title: Barnsley Hospital NHS awards ambient voice contract
items.summary: Barnsley Hospital NHS Foundation Trust has awarded a contract for ambient voice technology acute licenses, set to run from November 2026 to February 2028, to Lyrebird Health.

items.title: Heidi Health takes decision to cut workforce by 18 percent
items.summary: Heidi Health has announced the decision to cut its workforce by 18 percent globally, pointing to “difficult choices” around where to focus teams and investment. In a message from co-founder and CEO Tom Kelly, the company shared that the announcement had been made to its workforce during an “all hands”

items.title: Maidstone and Tunbridge Wells shares plans for outpatient, diagnostic, remote care innovation
items.summary: Maidstone and Tunbridge Wells NHS Trust has shared plans for outpatient and diagnostic transformation, remote care, and digital innovation in its latest trust strategy to 2031, aiming to reshape the way care is delivered, optimise existing digital systems, and embrace new digital opportunities.

items.title: Funding approval for EPR at North West Anglia NHS
items.summary: North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust (NWAFT) has reportedly received confirmation of funding for a new EPR system, allowing work to move ahead on an outline business case, with a target date for implementation of 2029.

items.title: New technology to spot illness years earlier gets UKRI backing
items.summary: UKRI backing for projects including cough-listening apps, an AI wellbeing coach for heart disease and routine eye scans that detect diabetes.

items.title: NHS workforce plan being reassessed due to AI advances, says health secretary
items.summary: The NHS workforce plan has been delayed again because advances in AI has caused the Government to reassess staffing numbers, the health secretary has said.

items.title: Digital Health and Care Wales abandons £10m AVT procurement
items.summary: Digital Health and Care Wales has chosen to abandon its £10m ambient voice technology procurement, citing a “limited number of suppliers successfully meeting the Conditions of Participation requirements”.

items.title: George Eliot Hospital revises plans for delayed EPR go-live in 2027
items.summary: A revised programme plan has been prepared by George Eliot Hospital NHS Trust, following a decision to delay the go-live of its EPR from October 2026 to August 2027.

items.title: AI software installed on over half of compatible NHS MRI scanners with DHSC noting opportunities to upgrade
items.summary: AI software is now installed on more than half of compatible NHS MRI scanners, the UK government has shared. The technology, along with the introduction of 125 new CT and MRI scanners, has been credited with playing a role in delivering one million more scans per year.

items.title: International: New York legislation for EHR organ donation integration, Korea and Mongolia partner on digital transformation, Meta offers $2 million
items.summary: For our latest international news in brief, we take a closer look at some of the stories to have caught our eye over the last few weeks from across the globe.

items.title: Agilent completes its acquisition of digital pathology software company Proscia
items.summary: Agilent closed the deal on 04/11/2026, paying $240 million in cash at closing with up to a further $30 million tied to future performance milestones. Proscia now sits in Agilent's Life Sciences and Diagnostics Markets Group. The deal was announced on 13/10/2026. No UK statement.

items.title: Turning investment into NHS impact: EBO’s next chapter
items.summary: Turning investment into NHS impact: EBO’s next chapter 3 November, 2026 For someone waiting for an appointment, a simple question can carry a great deal of importance. When will I be seen? Where do I need to go? Is there something I should do beforehand? Can I reschedule?

items.title: Torbay and South Devon NHS FT digital-first, AI and future of neighbourhood health
items.summary: The publication of Torbay and South Devon NHS Foundation Trust’s plan for better care has acknowledged progress to date for digital first and AI, with metrics on current use of digital tools and systems such as MyCare, Copilot, and Epic.

items.title: HTN Now 2027 schedule: NHS Online Trust, EPRs, AVT, digital inclusion, workforce skills, neighbourhoods
items.summary: HTN is delighted to share our initial HTN Now webinar schedule for 2027, where we will be sure to share digital and health tech projects, learnings, approaches and best practices across health and care! The webinars are FREE for NHS professionals – you can register your front row seat here.

items.title: South West Yorkshire Partnership highlights digital medicines, AVT and regional EPR procurement
items.summary: The board of South West Yorkshire Partnership Teaching NHS Foundation Trust has highlighted work on digital medicines, digital systems, and AVT, along with its role leading regional EPR procurement.

items.title: Radiotherapy research strategy for the North West sets out actions for data, AI and digital systems
items.summary: The North West Radiotherapy Network, made up of The Christie NHS Foundation Trust, The Clatterbridge Cancer Centre NHS Foundation Trust, and Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; has published a research strategy setting out priority actions for data, AI, automation, and digital systems over the next…

items.title: North West London Acute Provider Group updates on digital and data plans for 2026/27
items.summary: North West London Acute Provider Group has shared an update on its digital and data plans for 2026/27, noting efforts to improve data sharing and reshape strategic objectives to focus on patient and staff experiences with technology, AI, automation, EPR, and the federated data platform.

items.title: Clatterbridge Cancer Centre digital systems investments, data and workforce digital learning
items.summary: The board of Clatterbridge Cancer Centre has discussed its current position and future plans on digital systems, data, and digital workforce capability and training.

items.title: West of England collaboration launches £50k innovation grant fund
items.summary: A collaboration in the West of England between Bristol NHS Foundation Trust, the University of the West of England, Sirona Care & Health, and Health Innovation West of England, has launched a £50k innovation grant fund designed to support improvements across the region.

items.title: AVT, Copilot and next phase of EPR at York and Scarborough Teaching Hospitals
items.summary: The board of directors of York and Scarborough Teaching Hospitals has discussed its use of ambient voice technology, Copilot, and the next phase of the EPR.

items.title: X-on Health offers support to GP practices affected by Silicon Practice shutdown
items.summary: X-on Health is offering up to three months’ free access to digital patient support and online consultation tools to help GP practices maintain patient access following Silicon Practice entering administration.

items.title: Spike in demand to nurse advice line leads to AI launch
items.summary: A gynaecological cancer charity has launched an artificial intelligence (AI) tool to ease pressure on its specialist nurses amid a dramatic increase in demand.

items.title: HTN Now panel deep dive into artificial intelligence for NHS trusts
items.summary: HTN was joined by an expert panel including Neill Crump, group associate director for innovation and partnerships at Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals and The Dudley Group, and Sameer Gangoli, clinical and governance lead for AI at University Hospitals Sussex, to discuss AI in healthcare.

items.title: Chancellor announces new AI review for NHS workforce
items.summary: A new review by the government into artificial intelligence (AI) and its potential uses for the health service workforce in England has been announced.

items.title: Budget 2026: Sovereign AI, NHS AI and productivity review, funding
items.summary: With the publication of the latest budget for 2026, the government has reaffirmed its commitment on AI for productivity, increasing opportunities for sovereign AI, AI for biosecurity, and exploring quantum technologies. “The government is ensuring its investment into the NHS is spent wisely,” it states.

items.title: 10-year UK pharmacy strategy outlines plans for digital training, AI, data sharing and tech for research
items.summary: A 10-year strategy for UK pharmacy has set out a shared vision to make research “an integral, accessible and inclusive part of every pharmacist’s and pharmacy technician’s career”.

items.title: 14 urgent care schemes to receive share of £140m to help tackle winter pressures
items.summary: £140 million in funding will be invested in 14 new urgent care schemes across England to help tackle winter pressures, the government has announced, aiming to increase capacity and improve patient flow. These schemes include ED improvements, new urgent treatment centres, and enhancements to digital systems.

items.title: Insight: Progress to electronic patient records in Wales
items.summary: HTN Insight: Progress and challenges with the move to electronic patient records in Wales What does the transition to digital records and electronic systems look like across Wales? What are the challenges, opportunities, and programmes underway, and what progress is being made?

items.title: Mid Cheshire rolls out AVT following successful trial
items.summary: Mid Cheshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust has rolled out ambient voice technology across more locations and community services following a successful trial. The initial trial of the Lyrebird AVT solution incorporated services including same day emergency care, dermatology, rheumatology, and urology.

items.title: Digital Health and Care Wales shares improvements to NHS Wales women’s health website
items.summary: Digital Health and Care Wales has shared details of improvements made to the NHS Wales women’s health website, incorporating feedback from users and introducing new functionality to make it easier for women to find local support.

items.title: £80 million outlined in NHS England market engagement for multi-neighbourhood training hubs
items.summary: NHS England has launched a preliminary market engagement exercise aiming to identify potential suppliers to support the future commissioning of multi-neighbourhood training hubs for primary care, with a total value of £80 million.

items.title: Epic launches integration for healthcare apps
items.summary: Epic has announced the release of new capabilities allowing app developers to build “connectors” linking other apps to Epic, and to support surfacing information stored elsewhere without switching between apps or portals.

items.title: Berkshire Healthcare selects digital MSK service supplier
items.summary: Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust has selected Flok Health to supply digital MSK triage and management services, at a total cost of £400k.

items.title: King’s College Hospital and Guy’s and St Thomas’ report £4.1 million in savings from EPR
items.summary: King’s College Hospital and Guy’s and St Thomas’ have reported savings of £4.1 million from their combined use of the Epic EPR system. The trusts point to the avoidance of 3.3 million duplicate or repeat tests, saving up to 275,000 hours of nursing and phlebotomy time since 2023.

items.title: NVIDIA invest in Doctolib healthcare AI
items.summary: NVIDIA has made an investment into Doctolib to support the health tech supplier develop artificial intelligence solutions and models for healthcare teams and patients.

items.title: Five AI tools approved for identifying prostate cancer on MRI scans
items.summary: Five artificial intelligence tools for more accurately detecting prostate cancer in MRI scans have been approved for use on the NHS. NICE said the tools have the potential to act like a ‘second pair of eyes’, helping radiologists review prostate MRI scans and improve accuracy and consistency of diagnosis.

items.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies to help detect prostate cancer on MRI
items.summary: HealthTech guidance — Draft guidance. Closes 12/11/2026.

items.title: HTN Now: Cyber resilience in the NHS, impact of AI and emerging tech challenges, preparing for 2027
items.summary: HTN was joined by Julian Wiggins, solutions director at Rackspace Technology, and Nasser Arif, cyber security manager at London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust and Hillingdon Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, for a recent webinar on the topic of cyber resilience.

items.title: North East Ambulance Service strategy looks to “the road ahead” with tech, data and AI
items.summary: North East Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust is looking to “the road ahead” in its latest trust strategy, recognising the increasing role that tech, data, and AI will play in shaping urgent and emergency care delivery.

items.title: Feature: Making security the easy choice: Protecting mobile devices in clinical environments
items.summary: This Cybersecurity Awareness Month, Daniel Johnston, MRes, RN, Director Clinical Operations International at Imprivata, discusses how mobile devices can improve clinical care and why getting security right is essential for protecting data, systems, and patients.

items.title: Feature: Closer to home, why community digital is the missing link
items.summary: By Gary Mooney, clinical solution executive at InterSystems Margaret is 84, she lives alone with frailty and heart failure. She is admitted to her local hospital by ambulance after a fall for the third time this year.

items.title: DHSC guidance on digitising adult social care, managing IT suppliers, using AI
items.summary: New DHSC guidance on digitising adult social care has tackled how services can be fully digital, adopt AI, manage IT suppliers, and introduce digital champions.

items.title: Digital patient monitoring system among innovative projects to improve cancer services across the Humber
items.summary: Humber and North Yorkshire Cancer Alliance has awarded a share of £135,000 to three projects run by Humber Health Partnership aiming to improve cancer services and outcomes for patients.

items.title: Developing digital health capability in neuroscience nursing: moving beyond assumptions
items.summary: British Journal of Neuroscience Nursing, Volume 22, Issue 5, Page 232-233, October 2026.

items.title: Single patient record could remove need for patient consent to share GP data, BMA warns
items.summary: The proposed NHS single patient record risks removing requirements to seek patients’ consent to share GP data, the BMA has warned. The union urged peers in the House of Lords to amend the Health Bill to ensure the common law duty of confidentiality continues to apply to medical records.

items.title: Barts Health and Guy’s and St Thomas’ funding for AI digital twins of human tissue
items.summary: An AI project from PharosAI, a collaboration between Barts Health NHS Trust, Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust, Queen Mary University of London (QMUL), and King’s College London (KCL), has received funding from Innovate UK to explore the potential to develop digital twins of human tissue.

items.title: The Christie shares impact of AVT on patient experience
items.summary: The Christie NHS Foundation Trust has shared updates on its use of ambient voice technology, offering an insight into how it is being used to support the patient experience.

items.title: Delegate registration opens for HTN X
items.summary: HTN is delighted to open delegate registration for HTN X, an event to discuss, participate, challenge and focus on emerging technologies, AI, automation, innovation, data, and future tech for health and care executives leading the future.

items.title: £5 million cancer innovation programme open call launches
items.summary: The fourth round of the NHS Cancer Programme Innovation Open Call has opened for applications, with funding of up to £5 million on offer for innovations to support earlier diagnosis and treatment.

items.title: NHS England opens £6.7 million secondary care medicines data pre-market engagement
items.summary: NHS England has opened a secondary care medicines data pre-market engagement, with high level objectives around achieving a reporting function on stock and daily issuance of medicines in secondary care, and a price comparison tool.

items.title: Northamptonshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust — NHFT Integrated Sexual Health Electronic Patient Record (EPR) PME (C484439)
items.summary: Procurement of software that is specifically designed to support Sexual Health services and aligns with the requirements of the British Association for Sexual Health and HIV (BASHH). Responses by 30/10/2026 17:00.

items.title: Patients prefer human medical advice over immediate AI
items.summary: The majority of patients prefer to wait for medical advice from a healthcare professional, rather than getting it immediately from AI, according to a new study out this week.

items.title: HTN Now: Digital and delivering neighbourhood health
items.summary: For a recent HTN Now webinar on the role of digital in delivering neighbourhood health, HTN was joined by an expert panel including Fay Johnstone, acute virtual ward matron at Maidstone and Tunbridge Wells (MTW) NHS Trust; Mayur Vibhuti, chief digital, data and intelligence officer at Kent and Medway…

items.title: Essex ICB outlines role of digital in 2026/27 system winter plan
items.summary: The latest winter plan for 2026/27 from Essex ICB has explored the role of digital and data across its system coordination centre, neighbourhoods, PCNs, ambulance services, virtual wards, and Hospital @ Home.

items.title: HTN Now Awards open for entries!
items.summary: HTN is delighted to launch the HTN Now Awards – for health tech innovators, healthcare teams, partnerships and suppliers to showcase how they’re making an impact!

items.title: Feature: Building the foundations for an effective single point of access
items.summary: A single point of access should not be just a front door, it should be part of a pathway redesign strategy. By Dr Tom Oakley, CEO, Feedback Medical The NHS is investing significant effort into implementing elective single points of access (SPoAs).

items.title: MHRA 2030 strategy vows to reduce regulatory barriers and create modern framework for AI as a medical device
items.summary: In its newly published 2030 strategy, the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has vowed to reduce regulatory barriers for UK start-ups and SMEs, develop a modern regulatory framework for AI as a medical device, and move forward with plans for the use of AI in transforming medicines development.

items.title: Airedale NHS FT prepares for EPR go-live
items.summary: Airedale NHS Foundation Trust is preparing to go live with its new Oracle Health Millennium EPR this weekend. In January, the trust noted additional capital and revenue pressures versus the EPR’s business case, with the programme given an overall rating of amber in the board assurance framework.

items.title: £9.9 million contract awarded for NHS Online Trust digital and data services
items.summary: NHS England has awarded a contract with a total value of £9.9 million to Kainos Software Limited for support with a range of services in preparation for the new NHS Online Trust.

items.title: AI-generated patient complaints adding to GP practice workload, survey finds
items.summary: Almost half (45%) of GP practice managers say AI-generated patient complaints are increasing workloads and affecting staff wellbeing and morale, according to a survey by the Medical Protection Society. The poll of almost 160 UK practice managers found just 7% said they had not encountered an AI-generated complaint.

items.title: Integrating artificial intelligence in oncology nursing for patients receiving chemotherapy: a review article
items.summary:
Background:
Artificial intelligence has the potential to improve symptom management and enable early intervention for patients receiving chemotherapy.


Aims:
To review applications of artificial intelligence in oncology nursing for chemotherapy-related symptom management, focusing on benefits…
